title: Split digraphs a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e
examples: Teacher, what is the silent e doing to the word cape?
When do I add a silent e to a word?

explain.say: Listen to the word cap. Say cap. The a makes a short sound.

draw.text: Split digraphs a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e

explain.say: Now add an e to the end. The word becomes cape. Say cape.
The a now makes a long sound. It says its name, a.
The e at the end is silent. It works with the a to make one sound. This is a split digraph.
Now try hop. Add an e, and it becomes hope. The o says its name.
It works with i and u too. Kit becomes kite. Tub becomes tube.

faq.q: Why is the 'e' silent in these words?
faq.a: The e makes no sound of its own. It works with the vowel before it, so that vowel says its name.
asks: Does the e make any sound?

faq.q: Does this happen with all vowels?
faq.a: Yes, this pattern works for all five vowels: a, e, i, o, and u. You must add the e to make the change.
asks: Can I use this with every letter?

faq.q: If I write it, do I always add the e?
faq.a: When you are spelling, you must remember to write the silent e to get the long vowel sound. It is a spelling rule.
asks: Do I always write the e?

faq.q: What is the difference between reading and spelling this?
faq.a: When you read, you see the split digraph and say the long sound. When you spell, you write the silent e at the end.
asks: How is reading different from writing?
Do I sound it out or write it?

faq.q: Can I use this rule with two vowels together?
faq.a: This rule is for one vowel followed by a silent e. Two vowels together usually make a different sound pattern.
asks: Does this work with two vowels?

facts: The silent e works with a vowel to make a split digraph, like a_e in cake.
It makes the vowel before it say its long sound.
For example, 'kit' becomes 'kite' with a silent e.
This pattern helps us read and spell long vowel sounds.

quiz.say: Look at the picture. Tap the word that names it.
quiz.why: Kite has a long i sound. The split digraph i_e makes it.

wrong.0: Kit has a short i sound, so add an e at the end.
wrong.2: The e goes after the t, at the end of the word.

quiz.say: Read hop. Which letter turns it into hope?
quiz.why: Adding e makes hope. The o now says its name.

wrong.0: Adding a makes hopa, which is a made-up word.
wrong.1: Adding i makes hopi, which is a made-up word.

quiz.say: Look at the picture. Tap its spelling.
quiz.why: Bone has a long o sound. The split digraph o_e makes it.

wrong.1: Bon has a short o sound, so add an e after the n.
wrong.2: The e goes at the end, after the n.
